static_average_effect.dgp: Y = 2*T + 2*Z + epsilon; epsilon has zero mean within every (T,Z) cell
static_average_effect.unidentified_atom: valid reverse-causal DAG Y -> T; no admissible backdoor adjustment

static_response.dgp: continuous T on a symmetric grid of 100 levels in [-2, 2]; each level has four rows Z = 0.5*T +/- 0.5 and Y = 1 + 2*T + 1.5*Z +/- 0.05 (all four sign pairs), so the within-level deviations cancel exactly
static_response.atoms: same masks as static_average_effect over [t, y, z]: T -> Y; Z -> T, Z -> Y, T -> Y; Y -> T (unidentified)
static_response.frequentist_tolerance_note: response.kennedy_dr (curve) and the GAM plug-in behind response.intervention_gcomp (level) smooth the exact linear law; observed atom deviations are at most 0.04 (level) and 0.013 (curve), well inside the 0.375 gap between atoms
static_response.note: direct atom: E[Y | T=t] = 1 + 2.75t; Z-adjusted atom: E[Y | do(T=t)] = 1 + 2t + 1.5*mean(Z) = 1 + 2t; conditional_on_identified = (0.5*direct + 0.3*adjusted) / 0.8 = 1 + 2.46875t; only the Frequentist scalar InterventionResponse aggregate carries a joint-IF SE (row-aligned atom influences); curves and Bayesian aggregates withhold the multi-atom interval, so this is a numeric pin, not a coverage claim
